comment: The `exports` edge, one row per OPERAND of an `export` statement. Every spelling the statement has is asserted, and the two negative halves are the ones a name-collecting reader fails: the `except` operands must NOT be published, and a `*`-marked declaration must NOT acquire an `exports` edge (its visibility is already published as `visibility: public` + `metadata.exported`, which is a different fact stated by a different carrier).

expectRelationships.comment: `export foo, Bar` — a bare operand is published by its own name. Confidence 1.0: the statement names it outright, with no inference and no name matching
the second operand of the same expression_list
`export hidden except …` — the operand BEFORE `except` is the re-export; the two after it are the exclusion

a qualified operand is published by its LEAF, because the store resolves an endpoint by matching it against a symbol name and R10 requires the spelling the lane gives its own symbols. The written form is kept in nimQualifiedName, the two-part record the f# lane writes for `System.IDisposable`
`export Payload as Renamed` renames LOCALLY; what leaves the module is still `Payload`, so `Renamed` is the alias carried beside it and never the endpoint
a `/`-separated operand is a MODULE, not a symbol, and is published whole — the same spelling the `imports` reader gives that module, so the two readings of one module are one target in the graph

a bare identifier that names an imported module is indistinguishable from one that names a local symbol without cross-file context, so it is published as written and carries no module marker. Recorded as a resolution finding, not guessed at

expectExports.name: hidden
expectExports.comment: the importable-unit list keeps the names THIS FILE PROVIDES. `hidden` is declared here, so `export hidden` re-publishes a unit this module is the provider of — the ordinary Nim idiom for widening a private proc to a public one, and the one thing `except` qualifies

expectExports.name: Payload
expectExports.comment: published under its own name; `Renamed` is the local alias and never enters the list, because no importer can bind `Renamed` from this module

forbidExports.name: foo
forbidExports.comment: PROVIDER semantics. `export foo` where `foo` is declared in another module is a name somebody ELSE provides; listing it in this module's importable-unit set would give one name two providers. The re-export is still published — as the `exports` RELATIONSHIP asserted above — because 'this module hands this name onward' is true whoever declares it

forbidExports.name: Parser
forbidExports.comment: the same rule for the qualified spelling, whose endpoint is the leaf: `common_parser.Parser` is provided by common_parser, not here

forbidExports.name: strutils
forbidExports.comment: a re-exported module is provided by the module it names

forbidExports.name: std/os
forbidExports.comment: a `/` path is the provider itself

forbidExports.name: helper
forbidExports.comment: the withheld half, restated on the importable-unit carrier: `export hidden except helper` means `helper` does NOT leave this module, so it must not be in the list of units an importer can bind

forbidExports.name: another
forbidExports.comment: the second operand of the same `except_clause`

forbidRelationships.comment: THE regression this fixture exists for. `except` names what does NOT leave the module, so publishing `helper` states the inverse of the construct. A reader that collects every identifier under `export_statement` passes every positive row above and still fails here. Corpus evidence that the form is real: nim/compiler/nifstreams.nim withholds nine names this way
the second operand of the same `except_clause` — one forbid per withheld name, so dropping the whole clause and dropping one name are different failures

the `*` marker is NOT the `export` statement. `proc visible*()` is published as `visibility: public` + `metadata.exported`, persisted into brain_symbol.visibility and already read by gravity (28,900 exported_symbol nodes in 1,335 corpus files). A second edge would restate it at ~17.6% payload growth for no query a reader could not already ask
an alias is a LOCAL name. The module publishes `Payload`; nothing named `Renamed` exists outside it, so an endpoint spelled `Renamed` would not resolve to any symbol

the neighbouring-label half of question 4: `import std/strutils` is an `imports` edge, `export strutils` is an `exports` edge. A reader that filed both under one of the two would satisfy a looser expectation and be wrong here.\n\nThis row used to forbid `imports -> strutils`, and it is RETARGETED to `foo` because that forbid became UNSATISFIABLE rather than false. `reexport.nim` line 41 is `import std/[strutils, os]`, so a real `imports` edge to the module `strutils` exists and must exist; the old row would have failed against a correct analyzer. The discriminator is unchanged in kind: `foo` is published ONLY by `export foo, Bar` and is imported by nothing, so an implementation that filed that re-export under `imports` still fails here. Choosing a target the language cannot also produce as an import is what keeps the check satisfiable by a correct implementation.
